title: Huaihai Campaign
summary: From 6 November 1948 to 10 January 1949 the Communist People's Liberation Army fought Nationalist forces around Xuzhou, between the Huai River and the Longhai railway, and destroyed most of the Nationalists' remaining elite armies. It left Nationalist units on the central front able to do little more than delay the Communist advance toward the Yangtze.

uncertainty.note: A US State Department memorandum counts the battle for Hsuchow from 9 November 1948; Chinese accounts date the campaign from 6 November.

as_recorded.value: the start of the battle for Hsuchow on November 9, 1948

where.modern_name: Xuzhou, Jiangsu, China (fighting spread between Xuzhou and the Huai River)
where.historical_name: Hsuchow (Xuzhou), Jiangsu Province, Republic of China

importance.justification: One of the three decisive campaigns of the Chinese Civil War; it destroyed the Nationalists' main central forces and opened the Yangtze to the PLA.

related.because: The collapse of Nationalist forces at Xuzhou left Nanjing and Shanghai exposed and made Communist victory on the mainland near certain.

sources.title: The Concept of Operations for the Huai-Hai Campaign (Selected Works of Mao Tse-tung, vol. 4)

reviewer_note: Least sure of the loss figure: over 555,000 Nationalist troops is the Chinese Communist figure (Mao's Selected Works editorial note and China Daily); no independent count was opened. The start date (6 November) comes from China Daily only; the US memo counts from 9 November.
author: historian-agent:o-s8

beats.caption: The People's Liberation Army opened a campaign of about two months against Nationalist forces around Xuzhou on 6 November 1948.
Chinese accounts count over 555,000 Nationalist troops wiped out; the campaign ended on 10 January 1949.
By 7 January 1949 a US memorandum judged remaining central-front Nationalist units too weak to do more than delay Communist aims.
